newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch power cut strands hundreds in trains, lifts.
newsitem.headline: Dutch power cut strands hundreds in trains, lifts.

text.p: Hundreds of train passengers were left stranded for several hours and people were trapped in lifts as a power failure threw the heart of the Netherlands into chaos on Monday.
Police said about one million people in the central province of Utrecht and nearby areas were affected when electricity supplies were cut off in the morning.
"There's been a lot of chaos," a police officer said.
The cause of the interruption was not known but a spokeswoman for the regional power authority REMU said the problem started at power stations in a neighbouring province.
"Some measures were taken to prevent the whole country going down," she added.
By early afternoon, electricity supplies had been restored to parts of Utrecht but full train services had still not resumed.
Dutch state rail company NS said hundreds of passengers were left stranded when dozens of electric trains ground to a halt midway through the morning.
NS officials said passengers had to wait up to several hours, and some even had to walk along railway tracks to reach diesel-powered trains and buses to resume their journeys.
NS spokesman Marco van Bekkum said hundreds of trains were affected, and services were unlikely to be back to normal for the evening rush hour.
In Utrecht, fire officers were called to several buildings to rescue people trapped inside lifts, while police officers had to direct traffic by hand as traffic lights went out.
But emergency services reported no injuries during the outage.

Utrecht-based co-operative bank Rabobank, one of the largest companies in the province, said its main computer network and dealing room continued operating using emergency power but office equipment did not work.
"The vital central functions were working," bank spokesman Jan Dost said.
